parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need for a full tqdm package, the repo-root `tqdm.tqdm.*` import style, metadata, examples, benchmarks, documentation helpers, package installation, and evaluator-aligned tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept core alias, pyproject, wheel, and test-suite ownership while a workflow delegated four auxiliary authoring trees and then two verifier checks.
parallel.implementation: It copied upstream tqdm 4.67.1, modified alias machinery and version/build config, accepted child-authored examples, meta tooling, benchmarks, and root metadata, and produced an installable artifact.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent integrated the workspace into a wheel and artifact containing the package, examples, metadata, tests, and build outputs before official evaluation.
parallel.verification: The parent saw 142 upstream tests pass, 142 alias tests pass, CLI checks pass, and a wheel build succeed; one verifier child passed import checks, but verifier workflow closure did not finish.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow verifier phase and two strict background test commands were killed before returning complete reports; official evaluation still passed.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same tqdm project obligations, including aliases, examples, metadata, benchmarks, optional integrations, packaging, and CLI behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor handled source copying, package changes, examples and metadata population, test adaptation, package data, wheel checks, and final smoke tests without delegation.
serial.implementation: It copied upstream source and extra repository assets, implemented a `tqdm.tqdm` shim, adapted examples and metadata trees, fixed pandas compatibility, and adjusted package discovery and data.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor cleaned stale build artifacts, rebuilt the wheel, installed it into a temporary target, and verified package imports and CLI execution from the installed wheel.
serial.verification: It ran upstream tests, alias tests, optional dependency checks, pandas 2.3.3 full suite, alias full-dependency suite, wheel build, wheel install, import, and CLI smoke tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: A final editable install in a venv was killed with exit 137 after stronger wheel and suite evidence had already passed; no official task requirement remained failing.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same project obligations and also explicitly exercised optional dependency and pandas behaviors later in the run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference explains the official result; both completed enough required behavior to pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split core work to the parent and auxiliary work to workflow author children, followed by two workflow verifier children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation, integration, verification, and packaging under the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used productive delegation but introduced a verifier lifecycle boundary; serial avoided that boundary by doing checks locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow brief specified shared task context, import paths, ownership boundaries, allowed files, and verification expectations for child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child interfaces; the main actor maintained all context and interface decisions directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no proven missing brief or cross-agent contract; the material boundary is verifier completion timing, not context loss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel copied upstream source, edited alias/version/build files, incorporated child-authored auxiliary trees, and built a wheel.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied upstream source and extra repo assets, implemented the alias shim and packaging, fixed pandas compatibility, and built a wheel.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on upstream-based implementations; serial spent more local effort on optional dependency compatibility while parallel used child-authored auxiliary trees.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Four author children returned, but the verifier phase was killed with both verifier agents still marked in progress and their raw logs interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and its verification evidence stayed directly in the main timeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an adverse child-result lifecycle interruption; serial avoided child join and return failure modes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child work targeted scoped trees and the final artifact included package, examples, metadata, tests, and build files without proven write collision.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same final project tree from one actor and cleaned stale build artifacts before final wheel validation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared workspace writes did not create an observable collision; serial's integration was simpler because only one actor wrote the final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel passed upstream tests, alias tests, CLI checks, and wheel build checks, but strict background checks and workflow verifiers did not finish before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial passed upstream tests, full pandas 2.3.3 tests, alias tests, wheel build, wheel install, import, and CLI smoke checks before the final killed venv check.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had a more complete local verification record, but both had enough evidence for the current official evaluator to pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out with process return code 143, killed strict background commands, and an aborted workflow verifier phase.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but only after local wheel install and CLI smoke checks; the killed command was an extra editable-venv validation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both hit the wall-clock budget, but the parallel timeout cut off active verifier children while the serial timeout cut off a later redundant check.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: both modes passed. The main difference is that the parallel run's workflow verifier phase was interrupted before complete verifier reports returned, while the serial run kept verification local and reached full suite, alias suite, wheel install, import, and CLI smoke evidence before its final extra venv command was killed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial pursued optional dependency and pandas compatibility more deeply; parallel had enough local and official evidence despite unfinished strict background checks.
Parallel relied on child-authored auxiliary trees, while serial implemented and verified the same surface in one main timeline.
evaluator_effects: Both status evaluations report solution_passed true even though quality passed counts exceed the listed total; the completed status evaluation is the controlling outcome record.

The child count is not itself a label, and the direct observed failure boundary is active verifier interruption, not excessive breadth consuming all budget before implementation.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The workflow state was killed with both verifier agents still in progress, and each verifier raw log ends with request interruption before a complete verifier report could return.
candidates.realized_consequence: Parallel lost complete verifier closure: the examples verifier and meta/bench verifier did not return final reports, and the parent also had two strict background checks killed before it closed.
candidates.near_match_reason: A verifier produced partial positive findings, but both verifier agents were still active and interrupted; the direct boundary is early termination before finalization rather than a completed verifier finding trapped below the parent.

candidates.reason: A complete package candidate was already built and verified; the interrupted verifier work was not an unpromoted final deliverable.
No child result was merged only after relevant verification without a later check; parent verification followed integration work.
The completed authoring child outputs were represented in the final tree; no completed implementation child was left unjoined.
This is the nearest rejected label, but the stronger directly observed transition is cancellation of active verifier children before finalization.
The same cancellation chain is already classified as early child termination; the parent had independent upstream, alias, CLI, wheel, and official acceptance evidence.
No concrete completed child result was available to the parent and then ignored at a decision point.
The parent was running and checking tests and outputs near timeout; the direct adverse event is interruption of active verifier children.
Concurrent children owned scoped trees, and no competing design across files required reconciliation.
No evidence shows two live agents editing the same file and observing or reconciling a concurrent change.
No source file created or owned by one agent was wholesale replaced by another live agent.
No required executable, entry point, or submitted artifact was overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
No broad promotion or cleanup replaced another agent's final-tree work or invalidated provenance.
Although children wrote a shared workspace, scoped ownership and the final passing artifact show no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem.
No generated artifact, cache, fixture, or temporary path from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The parallel workflow was aborted with verifier children still active, and both verifier logs show request interruption before final reports. This produced partial verifier closure, while serial verification remained in the main timeline.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Parallel reached closure without complete workflow verifier reports and with two strict background test commands killed, reducing local verifier completeness though not changing the official pass result.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The evidence shows active verifier children were interrupted, so the more precise boundary is early termination before finalization rather than a completed verifier finding that failed to return.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Missing Verifier Return, Blind Timeout Wait, No Failure Takeover, Critical-Path Starvation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, and Oversized Child Task were considered around the same timeout chain and rejected because Early Child Termination is the direct boundary.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no context, owner, write, retry, or contamination pattern clears the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only one label is retained because the unfinished verifier evidence, killed background checks, and timeout symptoms are one lifecycle chain with one corrective boundary.
